features.description: Build tooling and baseline: site builds and a post page renders with title
steps: Run .harness/init.sh
Open http://127.0.0.1:4000/blog/pi-bench-harness-iterations/
Verify the post title h1 and body render

features.description: Post-UX asset scaffold: a custom SCSS partial and custom JS file are wired into every page

Add assets/js/post-ux.js loaded via _includes/footer/custom.html (defer)
Reload the post page and confirm the script loads with no console errors

features.description: Design tokens: a coherent type scale, spacing scale, accent color and content width defined as CSS variables for light mode
steps: Open a post
Verify headings, body, links and meta text use the shared tokens and look visually consistent

features.description: Readable body typography: comfortable measure (about 65-75ch), line-height ~1.7, paragraph spacing, and a font stack that renders Vietnamese diacritics well
steps: Open a Vietnamese post (e.g. the RSNA Knee wrap-up) at 1280px
Verify line length is not wider than ~75 characters in normal posts and diacritics render crisply
Verify heading hierarchy (h2/h3/h4) is clearly distinguishable

attempts.note: At 1280px on /blog/rsna-knee-abnormality-detection-wrap-up/ body p computed font-size is 19.125px (html scales up at xl breakpoint), max-width 70ch resolves to ~845px, and actual rendered line length is 72-88 chars/line (typically ~81) for Vietnamese paragraphs; step requires not wider than ~75 chars. Coder measured at 17px only. Fix: cap measure in a way that holds at larger root font sizes (e.g. ~60ch or max-width in em tied to char count, or set explicit font-size) and re-measure real chars/line. Other items OK: Inter loaded and applied, line-height 1.7, diacritics render, h2 33.75px/700 with border.

features.description: Click-to-zoom lightbox for images in post content

Click an image
Verify a full-size overlay opens, Esc or click closes it, and focus returns

features.description: Images lazy-load and have width/alt handling so layout does not jump
steps: Open a long image-heavy post with network throttling
Verify offscreen images carry loading=lazy and the page does not shift when they load

attempts.note: Lazy/decoding attrs present (6/6 content imgs on rsna wrap-up), alt ok. But layout-shift goal not met: built HTML imgs have no width/height and no CSS aspect-ratio; post-ux.js sets width/height only AFTER load, which is too late. An unloaded lazy img has 0 height (verified: new Image loading=lazy appended to .page__content measures height 0), so the page jumps when each image loads. Need dimensions reserved before load (e.g. build-time width/height or aspect-ratio via per-image data, or placeholder min-height).

features.description: Dark mode covers all post elements: code, tables, blockquotes, TOC, sidebar, related cards, images
steps: Enable dark mode
Scroll a post and verify every component has legible contrast with no white patches

attempts.note: Dark mode on /blog/rsna-knee-abnormality-detection-wrap-up/ (TOC present): .toc .nav__title 'On this page' is rgb(230,237,243) on rgb(31,111,235) = 3.92:1, below 4.5:1 (description: legible contrast). Coder audited only pi-coding-agent-setup which has no TOC. Fix: darken that bg or use darker TOC header. Everything else (no light patches, code, tables, images brightness .92, footer, related, share) passed on both posts.

features.description: Wide posts (classes: wide) keep a comfortable text measure while allowing wide figures, with TOC still working
steps: Open the RSNA Knee wrap-up (classes: wide)
Verify body text column is readable and wide images/tables can use extra width

attempts.note: At 1280px on rsna wrap-up, .page__content is 944px and images/tables/pre span the full 944px (x318-1262), but the sticky floated TOC (.sidebar__right.sticky, z-index 10, opaque bg, x1032-1262, ~1559px tall) sits on top of them: while scrolled (scrollY~13000) an img at y-249..459 overlaps the TOC rect and document.elementFromPoint at the overlap returns H4.nav__title, so the right ~230px (24%) of wide figures/tables is covered by the TOC. Expected: wide figures usable alongside a working TOC without occlusion. Text measure itself is fine (p 402px, ~62 chars/line, scrollWidth 1280).
